newsitem.title: USA: Apparel boosts U.S. retailers' November sales.
newsitem.headline: Apparel boosts U.S. retailers' November sales.

text.p: Strong apparel sales with fewer promotions gave holiday cheer to U.S. retailers' November sales, but industry analysts said consumer electronics continued to lag.
Calendar quirks made some year-to-year comparisons look negative as Thanksgiving was later this year, but analysts said on a week-by-week basis sales were strong.

"Everybody had been downplaying their expectations for November because of this calendar shift, and I actually think the numbers look pretty good," said Karen Sack, a retail analyst for Standard & Poor's.

Salomon Brothers, in a report, noted that an improving retail environment for apparel, coupled with easier comparisons, led to gains in November sales. Its same-store sales index for the month rose 3.9 percent, compared with 2.9 percent a year ago.
"Concurrently, we believe that lower levels of discounting and strong inventory and expense controls have positioned the major retailers well in terms of profitability," the Salomon analysts said.

Sears, Roebuck and Co, for example, said it posted record sales over the Thanksgiving weekend. Although sales at stores open at least a year fell 0.7 percent for the four weeks ended November 30, Sears said the month went according to plan.

"Sales were on plan for November given the fact that Thanksgiving was later this year," Sears chairman and chief executive officer Arthur Martinez said in a statement. "Record sales over Thanksgiving weekend produced an encouraging jump-start for a strong holiday shopping season at Sears."
The Thanksgiving holiday fell on November 28 this year, while last year it was November 23.
With the lack of a blockbuster product like last year's Windows 95, analysts said consumer electronics were lagging.
"I think it's going to end up being one of the best years in the last four for apparel, and for consumer electronics one of the worst," said Dean Ramos, a retail analyst for Dain Bosworth Inc.
Best Buy Inc, for example, reported its November same store sales fell eight percent versus last year. During the same period last year, comparable store sales rose 15 percent, the company said.

Sales for its fiscal third quarter were up four percent at $2.007 billion, but nonetheless below expectations, Best Buy said. "In addition, the personal computer category became more promotional in November," Allen Lenzmeier, chief financial officer, said in a statement.
